value.hook: Open before narrowing a registry/roster read, adding a read-only callerless route, holding a file open in the observer, or renaming a function a source-scan test names
value.title: Cutting daemon at-rest reads: trace predicates, never cache seats (F182, F184, F185)

sections.name: body
sections.value:
What took the daemon from about 33% to about 19% CPU at rest, and what to keep doing.

- **Never cache `seats`.** `store/orchestration.rs::reconcile_descriptors` writes `seats` directly, outside the Registry, and doesn't bump `seq`. A write-invalidated cache or a seq-keyed snapshot would go stale. Instead, narrow the read itself.
- **Narrow by tracing every predicate, then filter in SQL.** Read each `seats.iter()...` in the function and its helpers. If every row used is matched by one key, filter by it and keep `ORDER BY id`, so `find` and `min_by_key` pick the same row. Tools now in the port:
  - `SeatFilter.pane`: `resolve_seat` by pane;
  - `SeatFilter.live_only`: the observer, both binders, the native-receiver reconcile;
  - `Registry::list_related(&RelatedSeats)`: ids, session, pane or pid, for the F162 brake and the locked registration re-read. Its default filters `list()`, so fakes need nothing.
  The registry contract (fake and SQLite) pins `list_related` to `RelatedSeats::matches`. A new claim check that reads another kind of row must widen `RelatedSeats`.
- **Minting is the one check that needs the whole id space.** Use `first_free_id` (one `get` per candidate) under the lock; never a scan.
- **Tap sinks:** the fd is held in `TapState.held` and reopened only when dev/ino at the path changes. Trim truncates in place, so the same inode is kept. Proof by denial: chmod 0200 after the first drain, and new bytes must still drain.
- **Callerless reads (F184):** `READ_LEAVES` in `http/governance.rs` is the one allowlist, and `read()` takes no actor. A missing caller refuses `E-RS-NO-CALLER` (`details.code`).
- **Source-scan guards:** `anomalies_tests.rs::the_three_handlers_never_call_the_unbounded_tail` does `include_str!("governance.rs")` and finds functions by name. A rename breaks it in CI only, so grep `include_str!` for the file before renaming.
- **Receipts:** ask ocelot for the BEFORE sample (300 s window plus one 10 s sample) before changing anything. Take your own `ps -o time` over 60 s, `pij-rs --json ping | jq .data.spawns.total` twice, and `just spawn-rate --seconds 20`. The AFTER sample is only meaningful post-deploy; a private daemon has no busy panes or status lines. Otter routes it.
- **Stopping a shared-build run:** stop_bash can orphan its cargo and leave target.lock behind with a dead owner pid. Kill the orphan, then remove the lock only if `owner` names your dead pid.
